audits.title: A Re-Audit of the Assessment and Management of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorders Following Admission to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Alcohol history documented 45%; weekly quantity 22%; CIWA-R on admission 0.7%; referral to community alcohol services 3%

audits.intervention: Recommendations implemented after the original audit (not detailed)

cycle2.result: Alcohol history documented 81%; weekly quantity 8%; CIWA-R on admission 4.0%; referral to community alcohol services 7%

audits.other_findings: Gamma GT and magnesium checks on admission improved; induction teaching, CIWA-R training and a flow chart were recommended.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Baruah R, Hussain M, Buchan H. A Re-Audit of the Assessment and Management of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorders Following Admission to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S162-S162.

audits.title: AUDIT^2 – A Clinical Audit of the Alcohol Assessment and Management in the Southern Gambling Service – First Round Results
audits.standard: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care and Royal College of Physicians guidance: full AUDIT if AUDIT-C at least 5, brief intervention for scores 5–10, advice and signposting for 11 or more
audits.setting: Southern Gambling Service (outpatient gambling disorder service)

cycle1.result: AUDIT-C and EWAC completed 100%; full AUDIT 0%; brief intervention documented in 7% of higher-risk; 1 (25%) possibly dependent patient signposted; none given advice on avoiding abrupt cessation

audits.intervention: Recommended: full AUDIT for AUDIT-C 5 or more, staff upskilling in brief intervention, regional alcohol services directory, psychoeducation materials
audits.other_findings: 98 patients referred; all with scores of 11 or more had alcohol discussed in formulation and 75% an ICD-11 alcohol diagnosis.
audits.citation: Teixeira F, Sinclair J, Chamberlain S, Ioannidis K. AUDIT^2 – A Clinical Audit of the Alcohol Assessment and Management in the Southern Gambling Service – First Round Results. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S284-S285. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10689.

audits.title: AUDIT^2 – Identification and Management of Alcohol Use Problems in the Southern Gambling Service: A Full Audit Cycle
audits.standard: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care guidance and Royal College of Physicians guidance on alcohol assessment and management by risk bracket
audits.setting: Southern Gambling Service (specialist gambling disorder service), Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Full AUDIT completion 0%, brief interventions 7%, advice on safe alcohol reduction 0%.

audits.intervention: Previously implemented recommendations from the initial audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: AUDIT-C and EWAC 100%. Full AUDIT completed in 100% meeting criteria (55). Score 8 or above: brief intervention 18 (66.7%), formulation 20 (74%). Score 20 or above: advice on avoiding abrupt reduction 7 (70%), formulation 8 (80%). Signposting 7/10 (70%).

audits.other_findings: 124 of 301 referrals (41.2%) were accepted and assessed. Documentation consistency and staff education still needed.
audits.citation: Yousof Y, Ioannidis K, Teixeira F, Chamberlain S. AUDIT^2 – Identification and Management of Alcohol Use Problems in the Southern Gambling Service: A Full Audit Cycle. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S15-S16. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11181.

audits.title: Education and audit can improve the identification of excessive drinkers among medical inpatients.
audits.standard: Recording of quantitative alcohol history, CAGE questionnaire use and alcohol notification in discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Quantitative alcohol history in medical notes 175/792 (22%) and nursing notes 31/792 (4%); excessive drinkers identified 40/792 (5.1%).

audits.intervention: Training of junior medical and nursing staff, then feedback of results at a clinical audit meeting.

cycle2.result: After audit feedback: quantitative history in medical notes 241/497 (48%) and nursing notes 237/497 (48%); excessive drinkers identified 45/497 (9.1%); chi 2 for trend p < 0.0001 for notes.

audits.other_findings: After training alone (n=690) medical notes 242/690 (35%) and nursing notes 123/690 (18%). Little improvement in CAGE use or discharge summaries.
audits.citation: Dent T, Shepherd R, London M, Alexander G, Duff C. Education and audit can improve the identification of excessive drinkers among medical inpatients. Health Trends. 1995;27(3):92-97. PMID: 10154269.

audits.title: Enhancing Screening and Counseling for Alcohol Use Disorder in a Predominantly Hispanic Border Town Population With the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test-Concise (AUDIT-C).
audits.standard: USPSTF recommendation for routine alcohol screening in adults
audits.setting: Internal Medicine Residency Clinic, TTUHSC El Paso

cycle1.result: AUDIT-C not routinely used before the project.

audits.intervention: AUDIT-C integrated into the EMR and resident training in alcohol counselling.
audits.other_findings: Of 12 surveyed after counselling, 83% had never been counselled before and 75% found it helpful.
audits.citation: Brockman MJ, Trivedi B, Kattamuri L, Delgado F, Hechanova LA, Deoker A, et al.. Enhancing Screening and Counseling for Alcohol Use Disorder in a Predominantly Hispanic Border Town Population With the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test-Concise (AUDIT-C). Cureus. 2025;17(5):e84541. doi:10.7759/cureus.84541. PMID: 40546638.

audits.title: [A multicenter primary care study on alcohol consumption].
audits.standard: Recording of alcohol consumption in the last two years

cycle1.result: Only 24.8% of records documented alcohol consumption; 11 (2.8%) met criteria for at-risk drinking.

audits.other_findings: Causes of low recording analysed to design interventions.
audits.citation: Bueno Ortiz JM, Aubà Llambrich J, Altaba Barceló A, Boneu Castells M, Cabaco Reverte C, Manzano Sarciada A, et al.. [A multicenter primary care study on alcohol consumption]. Aten Primaria. 1997;19(2):80-83. PMID: 9147574.
